description: Seating Arrangement is an important topic of Logical Reasoning. It involves arranging persons or objects in a specific order or geometric shape based on given conditions.

sections.title: Basic Types
sections.description: The main geometric types of seating arrangement asked in competitive exams.

key_concepts.explanation: Arranging persons in one or more straight rows. This can be in a single row or in parallel rows.
Arranging persons around a circular table at equal distances from one another.
Arranging persons at the corners or in the middle of the sides of a rectangular or square table.

sections.title: Direction and Facing
sections.description: Correctly determining the right and left based on the direction the persons are facing is the most crucial part of this topic.

results: Facing North: Your right and left are exactly the row's right and left.
Facing South: Your right and left become the reverse of the row's left and right.

sections.title: Use of Connector Words
sections.description: It is essential to understand the correct meaning of connector words as they indicate which person the information refers to.

key_concepts.explanation: These words always refer to the first person in the sentence. Example: 'A is second to the right of B and is a neighbor of C', here 'and' refers to A.
These words always refer to the immediate preceding person. Example: 'A is second to the right of B who is a neighbor of C', here 'who' refers to B.

sections.title: Systematic Steps to Solve
sections.description: A logical approach to accurately solving complex seating arrangements.

steps.title: Draw the Basic Framework
steps.detail: Draw the correct geometric shape according to the given number of persons and mark all their seating positions.

steps.title: Place Definite Information
steps.detail: Start with the clues that state the exact position of a person (e.g., 'P sits at an extreme end').

steps.title: Connect Related Clues
steps.detail: Find linked information related to the persons you have already seated and fill them in the diagram.

steps.title: Use Negative Clues
steps.detail: Use information like 'A is not a neighbor of B' to eliminate wrong possibilities and fill in the remaining empty spaces.

sections.title: Special and Complex Cases
sections.description: Difficult patterns that often appear in high-level competitive exams.

cases.condition: Linear Arrangement of Unknown Number of Persons
results: Do not draw a fixed row at the beginning.
Add new positions one by one according to the conditions, and pay special attention to clues related to the extreme ends.
When professions or favorite colors are given along with the persons, you can use a small table alongside your diagram.
Write the variable clearly near each person's seated position to avoid confusion.
